name: Noncontained Sections Can Still Satisfy the Full Endpoint Law
statement: The explicit 872-concept noncontained-section rooted factor has the full sectionwise endpoint-transfer law despite failing the paired presentation containment hypotheses. Every unattainable vertex other than zero already fails in its own proper section, so zero is its unique critical root. This remains true after protecting the root and deleting all nonroot vertices of degree at most two, since there are none.
proof: Three explicit relative orders clear pairs of layers to the two side sections and the opposite section. The first two transfer every endpoint attainable in the corresponding side. The opposite section has one initial corner, after whose deletion its attainable endpoints are exactly those of the core, and the third relative order transfers them. Necessity follows by coordinate-face restriction. The recorded corner and degree census proves the root-protected graph-core assertion.
